gap: No result ChatGPT got names or prices a single power source that meets the Mini's 100 W USB-C PD need. Today the cheapest 100 W options on maker stores are the Baseus EnerFill FE11 100 W wall charger at $49.99 and the Baseus EnerFill FC41 20,000 mAh 100 W power bank at $59.99 (about 2 h of Mini runtime). The BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 (288 Wh, 140 W PD) is $299.99 and runs it for about 6–12 h.
standout_why: I compared against the three cited Starlink Help Center pages (a7fe6525 'How can I power my Starlink Mini?' and fba85643 'What USB power rating do I need', ws and gb copies) and the top results (Mini USB-C Cable article, accessories_guide_mini.pdf, Mini product page). All of them are Starlink's own pages. ChatGPT's answer built from them gives the requirement (USB-PD, 20 V, 100 W) and runtimes per Wh, but it names no charger, power bank or station and gives no prices. The starlink.com help pages are rendered by JavaScript and came back empty when I fetched them. I couldn't extract the accessory PDF's text. So I compared against ChatGPT's answer as the shopper saw it, which carried no products or prices.
decides: The answer gets a price ladder. A $49.99 100 W wall charger covers mains power. A $59.99 100 W bank covers about 2 h away from an outlet. A $299.99 288 Wh station with a 140 W USB-C port covers a full day, which matches our current page's pick of the Elite 30 V2 as the smallest all-day option. Anything at 65 W (Baseus GaN5 Pro 65W) or the 30 V 2 A (60 W) car boosters sold for the Mini is ruled out. Spending $115.99 on a 160 W charger gains nothing for the Mini over a 100 W one.
